correctness.rationale: For an active direction-i edge with ordered gap ℓ, two direct arc contributions are −2 c_i ℓ^(p−1), and each of q_i−2 other complete-fiber vertices contributes −c_i ℓ^(p−1)[s^(p−1)+(1−s)^(p−1)], whose minimum α_p=1 for p≤2 and 2^(2−p) for p>2 follows from concavity/convexity. Matched edges in any other coordinate j have nonpositive derivative difference by monotonic flux and same c_j. Hence the upper Dini derivative L_i ≤−κ_i L_i^(p−1). Permutation symmetry keeps zero direction seminorm zero, and scalar ODE comparison gives finite-time, exponential or power law envelopes. One-clique high/low or +/-/zero profiles realize equality and their additive product solves the full nonlinear equation because each edge increment is coordinate-separable. Thus all axes/times simultaneously saturate and extinction is sharp. Independently tested 168 weighted active-edge derivative inequalities and 28 sharp separable initial derivatives on small Hamming products; general proof is analytic.

value.rationale: Sharp nonlinear gradient regularization in each anisotropic coordinate is a natural observable for product Markov graphs; it supplies exact rates, globally simultaneous extremizers and optimal finite-time consensus in fast diffusion p<2. Neither general semigroup contraction nor textbook p=2 mixing alone gives the p-dependent piecewise sharp directional classification.

final_claim: For anisotropic finite Hamming graphs ∏ K_qi and common p>1, each coordinate edge-Lipschitz seminorm under nonlinear p-heat satisfies a scalar sharp differential envelope with κ_i=c_i[2+(q_i−2)α_p], simultaneously attained by one separable solution for every prescribed vector and all time; for p<2 finite consensus time is sharp.
limitations: Finite Cartesian complete graphs, common exponent p>1, per-axis constant positive conductances, unit masses; no arbitrary weighted edges, non-product graph or varying p_i; no two-solution contraction claim.
